# 4. Results

Five subsections, ~1300 words at draft stage; ms-writer will tighten to the final ~900–1100 needed for the NeurIPS body. Format follows §1 b_draft: numbered paragraphs (¶N) with topic sentence first, supporting prose retained from the §3 outline. Aron should curate, then hand to `ms-writer` for `_3-results.c_final.md`. Numbers cite `analysis/cell_summaries/*.csv`; figures live in `analysis/figures/`. Cells with insufficient data are flagged inline.*

## 4.1 Cross-model behavioural baselines (no-noise)

**¶1.** *The two models occupy distinguishable but no longer dramatically different no-noise regimes.* In the v4 direct-provider configuration with $T = 10$, mem-3, and the unconstrained `anything` myth topic, GPT-5-Nano reaches a mean cumulative dyad balance of **69.2** (median 71.0, std 4.6, $N=15$) in the game-only cell, with `game→myth` and `myth→game` cells slightly higher (71.1 and 72.3 respectively). Claude-Sonnet-4.5's matched v4 no-noise game-only cell is under-replicated ($N = 2$); pulling the corresponding numbers from the prior `baseline/` corpus gives a mean of 55.7 (median 55.0, std 2.6, $N = 15$). Maximum possible dyad reward is 150.

**¶2.** *This revises an earlier working assumption.* Pilot work with GPT-5-Nano routed through OpenRouter showed apparent floor-locking at mutual defection. In the direct-provider configuration the same model reaches roughly half the dyad ceiling without any noise intervention. The cross-model gap is therefore moderate (~14 points of dyad reward), not the chasm the pilot suggested. We retain Claude as the higher-cooperation regime and GPT-5-Nano as the more variable one, but both exhibit substantive cooperation under no-noise conditions.

**¶3.** *Variance reduction is visible even at baseline.* GPT-5-Nano's no-noise dispersion drops monotonically across task orders: std 4.6 in game-only, 2.7 in `game→myth`, 1.1 in `myth→game`. We mention this here because the same pattern recurs systematically under noise (§4.3), so the across-seed signature is not specific to the noise interventions.

## 4.2 Effect of noise on the cooperation profile

**¶4.** *Direction-of-noise dominates the noise effect.* Bidirectional summary across the four implemented mechanisms in v4: positive (uniform $+5$) noise pushes both models near the cooperation ceiling — Claude reaches a game-only mean balance of 73.5 (informed: 74.2), GPT-5-Nano reaches 72.5 (informed: 72.4). Negative (uniform $-5$) noise depresses Claude to 29.3 (informed: 30.4) but lifts GPT-5-Nano relative to its no-noise baseline, to 37.9 (informed: 38.4) — agents perceive losses as smaller than they are, sustaining trust longer.

**¶5.** *Bootstrap noise is qualitatively distinct.* Bootstrap noise replaces the trustee's returned amount with the maximum possible return every round, masking actual reciprocation. In v4, GPT-5-Nano's game-only mean under bootstrap noise is 66.6 (informed: 67.9) — moderate cooperation, well above no-noise. Bootstrap is therefore not just an "upward" noise variant; it removes the trustee-return signal entirely. This matters in §4.3.

**¶6.** *Informedness has not produced a large qualitative shift.* Across all noise mechanisms in v4, agents told that the channel is noisy still respond mainly to the realized ledger they observe; informed and uninformed cells differ by 1–2 points of mean cumulative reward across most cells. Treat informedness as a robustness check rather than a central manipulation in this version.

**¶7.** *Note on scope.* §4.1 and §4.2 use this paper's two direct-provider models. Gemini cells from the prior pilot are out of scope per §3.4. The effect of noise on Gemini's higher-cooperation baseline is left for the EMNLP follow-up.

## 4.3 Effect of myth-writing on game behaviour (the headline question)

**¶8.** *The myth effect is conditional on the noise regime, not universal.* Of 21 (model × noise × myth-order) cells in the v4 corpus, the bootstrap classification (Δmean and variance ratio CIs from `analysis/cell_summaries/deltas.csv`) gives: 3 lift+consolidation, 1 pure consolidation, 2 pure lift, 10 null, 2 harmful, 2 destabilizing, 1 missing. Six cells show some positive myth effect, four cells show a negative effect, and the remaining ten are null. **Lift+consolidation lives entirely in upward-noise cells; destabilization lives entirely in GPT-5-Nano × bootstrap noise.** Figure @fig-decision summarises the full classification.

![3×3 classification (mean shift × variance shift, bootstrap CIs) for every (model × noise × myth-order) cell. Green = positive myth effect, red = negative, gray = null/missing. Lift+consolidation lives in upward-noise cells; destabilization in GPT-5-Nano × bootstrap.](figures/fig_decision_table.png){#fig-decision width=100%}

**¶9.** *The strongest positive cells are upward-noise.* Three cells reach lift+consolidation classification (mean ↑, variance ↓, both CIs strict): (a) Claude × positive (informed) × `game→myth`: Δmean **+0.59 [+0.22, +0.96]**, variance ratio **0.31 [0.05, 0.66]**; (b) GPT-5-Nano × positive × `myth→game`: Δmean **+2.08 [+0.17, +4.44]**, variance ratio **0.05 [0.00, 0.54]**; (c) GPT-5-Nano × positive (informed) × `game→myth`: Δmean **+2.23 [+1.06, +3.52]**, variance ratio **0.08 [0.01, 0.24]**. The variance reductions are substantial — between 3× and 20× compared to the matched game-only cell.

**¶10.** *The negative cells are all GPT-5-Nano × bootstrap.* Four cells classify harmful or destabilizing: GPT-5-Nano × bootstrap × `game→myth` Δmean **−7.73 [−14.27, −1.67]**; × `myth→game` Δmean **−7.60 [−13.53, −2.07]**; × bootstrap (informed) × `game→myth` Δmean **−9.67 [−14.67, −5.00]** with variance ratio 7.5 [3.5, 15.8] (destabilizing); and (informed) × `myth→game` Δmean **−6.87 [−11.13, −3.07]** with variance ratio 4.8 [1.5, 11.0] (destabilizing). Adding myth-writing to a dyad already operating under reciprocity-flipping noise makes things measurably worse.

**¶11.** *Interpretation.* The upward-noise cells share a property: agents observe a perceived cooperation signal from their partner that is at least as positive as the underlying decision. Adding myth-writing in this regime yields a small mean lift and a substantial variance reduction — the dyad locks onto a coordination point. The bootstrap cells share the opposite property: agents observe a perceived signal that systematically *contradicts* the underlying interaction (full reciprocation reported regardless of actual return). Adding myth-writing here introduces a second structured prior that competes with the noisy reciprocation report; the dyad becomes less coherent. The "consolidation" interpretation from the §1 framing therefore needs a complement: under favourable noise, myth consolidates; under reciprocity-flipping noise, it destabilises.

**¶12.** *The remaining ten cells.* Negative-noise cells for both models show no detectable myth effect (10/10 classify null). This is a substantive and honest result — the myth channel has detectable effects only at the extremes of the noise design.

![Mean cumulative balance over rounds, faceted by (model × noise) with one line per task order. Shaded ribbons are ±1 std across seeds. The bootstrap-noise harm pattern is visible in the bottom row: gray (game-only) sits above blue/red (myth-present).](figures/fig_trajectories.png){#fig-trajectories width=100%}

## 4.4 Linguistic dynamics in the myth chain

**¶13.** *Between-agent embedding cosine convergence is robust across cells.* Pairwise cosine between Agent_1 and Agent_2 myths at the same round (sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2, normalized) shows a positive slope over rounds in **18 of 21 cells** (slope CI excludes 0 above; `analysis/cell_summaries/embedding_summary.csv`). The strongest cells are GPT-5-Nano × negative_5 × `myth→game` (slope **+0.027/round** [0.016, 0.038], cosine 0.42 → 0.74 across 10 rounds), GPT-5-Nano × bootstrap × `myth→game` (+0.023/round), and Claude × positive (informed) × `myth→game` (+0.021/round). This holds **even in cells where the game outcome is null or harmful**, so linguistic convergence is not contingent on behavioural improvement.

**¶14.** *Lag-1 cross-agent cooperativity correlations are positive in every cell.* Pearson r between Agent_A's cooperativity-lexicon score in their round-$t$ myth and Agent_B's in round $t+1$, computed per dyad and aggregated (`analysis/cell_summaries/lag_summary.csv`). Mean per-dyad max-direction r ranges 0.27–0.58 across cells, with **27–73% of dyads showing |r| > 0.5**. The strongest cell is GPT-5-Nano × positive (informed) × `myth→game`: lag1_max mean **0.58 [0.43, 0.71]**, 73% of dyads above 0.5. The pilot's Claude r ≈ 0.72 finding sits at the upper tail of a clearly non-zero distribution; it is representative, not anomalous.

**¶15.** *Coinages persist within myths but do not leak out.* A simple dictionary-based coinage detector (alphabetic, length ≥6, not in `/usr/share/dict/words` after suffix stripping; `analysis/cell_summaries/neologism_summary.csv`) finds that Claude produces 2–5 distinct coinages per chain, with maximum persistence reaching **all 10 rounds** for invented names like *Lumina*, *Aelara*, *Arachnis*, *Celestia*, *Luminara*. GPT-5-Nano produces more coinages (~5–6 per chain) but they persist for fewer rounds (~1.5–2). However, **share of runs in which any myth-coinage reappears in any agent's game `reason` text is 0.00, in every cell.** The pilot observation of coinage leakage from myth into game-reasoning text **does not replicate at corpus scale**. Coinages stay inside the myth.

## 4.5 Coupling between game behaviour and myth content

**¶16.** *The Claude reasoning prose is extensively threaded with own-myth vocabulary.* For each round we extract the agent's `game_responses[ag].content` field — the LLM's response to the trust-game prompt, including any reasoning prose it emits before the JSON action — and code it against the agent's own myth chain up to the previous round (`analysis/cell_summaries/reason_coding_summary.csv`). For Claude-Sonnet-4.5: **78–82% of round-level game responses contain at least one content word from the agent's own preceding myth**, with a mean of 5–7 unique vocabulary overlaps per response. **100% of Claude runs** have at least one such reference. Theme-lexicon hits (story / spirit / elder / sacred / ancestor / ritual / etc.) reach 10–33% of responses, with negative-noise cells showing the highest theme density.

**¶17.** *GPT-5-Nano emits no reasoning prose.* Across every (noise × task-order) cell in the v4 corpus, GPT-5-Nano's `game_responses[ag].content` is the bare JSON action (e.g. `{"send": 3}`, mean length ~12 characters) with empty `reasoning` field. The reason-coding metric is therefore 0.00 for every GPT-5-Nano cell — but this reflects model output behaviour, not absence of cross-task computation. **The cross-task linguistic channel is methodologically undecidable for GPT-5-Nano in this configuration.** This is a substantive limitation to flag in §5.5: the channel is observable for models that emit reasoning text alongside the action, and only those.

**¶18.** *Three layers of evidence for the linguistic channel.* Combining the linguistic findings: (a) between-agent embeddings systematically converge over rounds in 18/21 cells (§4.4); (b) cooperativity-lexicon scores transmit lag-1 between agents in every cell, often strongly (§4.4); (c) for Claude, myth-vocabulary content is present in essentially every game response (§4.5). The carriers are different — semantic embedding for (a), narrow lexical scoring for (b), thematic vocabulary for (c) — but all three point the same direction: the myth channel is doing measurable work.

**¶19.** *Why this matters for §4.3.* The cells where myth lifts and consolidates cooperation (Claude × positive (informed) × `game→myth`; GPT-5-Nano × positive × either myth order) are the cells where headroom exists *and* the linguistic channel is most active. The cells where it destabilises (GPT-5-Nano × bootstrap) are the cells where noise systematically contradicts the action signal, so an additional structured prior from the myth competes rather than cooperates. The §4.3 mean-and-variance picture is consistent with the §4.4–4.5 linguistic picture: language is doing real work, but its sign depends on whether it converges with or competes against the noise channel.

## 4.6 Tightening the cross-task channel — a 2×3 mechanism factorial

**¶20.** *The constrained-channel design of §3.3 leaves a clean follow-up: what happens when the channel is structurally opened?* In the implicit-channel design, the partner's myth reaches the game-side computation only via the agent's own previous myth-writing prompt — a thin channel. We added a **partner-myth injection** variant in which the partner's most recent myth is quoted verbatim inside the trust-game prompt, all GPT-5-Nano, run on the four noise conditions of §4.3.

**¶21.** *In the bootstrap-noise cells where myth was harmful, partner-myth injection reverses the destabilisation.* Bootstrap × `game→myth`: baseline anything-myth (no injection) Δmean −7.7 vs game-only baseline (mean 58.9, std 11.0); with injection Δmean +1.5 (mean 68.1, std 3.5). Same pattern in `myth→game` (Δmean −7.6 → +1.8; std 9.2 → 3.6). Across-seed variance collapses ~3×; mean cooperation returns to baseline. In the positive-noise cells where myth was already lifting (§4.3 ¶9), injection adds no detectable extra effect (Δmean change < 0.2 across all four positive cells). The intervention is **regime-conditional**: it acts only where the implicit channel was failing.

**¶22.** *To discriminate visibility from content, a follow-up factorial varied the myth topic across three directions.* Anything-myth (the unconstrained `anything` topic, neutral content), cooperative-themed (`reciprocity_oath`: a story about honoring reciprocal obligations), and adversarial (`trickster_exploitation`: a story about being exploited by a defector). Each crossed with the visibility manipulation (no injection vs partner-myth injection). 60 cells of fresh data, all GPT-5-Nano × bootstrap noise, $N = 15$ per cell.

**¶23.** *Visibility dominates content direction.* The 2×3 factorial on bootstrap × `game→myth` (uninformed):

| Content / visibility | No injection | + Injection |
|---|---|---|
| Anything (neutral) | 58.9 ± 11.0 (harmful) | **68.1 ± 3.5** (rescue) |
| Cooperative | 57.4 ± 12.4 (harmful) | **69.8 ± 2.9** (rescue) |
| Adversarial (defection-themed) | n/a | **66.6 ± 5.5** (rescue) |

All three injection cells land in the rescue zone (66–70); all two no-injection cells stay in the harmful zone (~58). Same pattern in `myth→game` and in the informed bootstrap variants. Cooperative content modulates the rescue marginally (~+2 over neutral); adversarial content modulates marginally downward (~−2). Content direction explains < 5% of variance; visibility explains the rest.

**¶24.** *Two further controls anchor the mechanism.* (a) A1 × **no-noise** baseline produces no effect (Δmean −0.8 to +0.9 across two cells, $N = 30$ runs, 0 failures), ruling out the alternative that injection just lifts cooperation by adding more partner-related text to the prompt — if that were the mechanism, no-noise cells would also lift. (b) An A1+A3 combination variant (partner-myth injection plus a system-prompt addendum requiring 2–3 sentences of reasoning before each JSON action) **erases A1's rescue** in the bootstrap cells (Δmean returns to ~−13 vs A1, std collapses further). Inspection of the prose shows GPT-5-Nano with forced reasoning surfaces explicit cost–benefit calculation rather than coordination; "net zero last round → send less" patterns dominate. The Claude reasoning-prose carryover finding (§4.5) may therefore be partly correlational: cooperative reasoning correlates with cooperative behaviour without necessarily causing it.

**¶25.** *Mechanism reading.* Under bootstrap noise, the trustee's actual return is replaced with the maximum possible return every round, so the agent observes a perceived reciprocation signal that systematically contradicts its own game-math. With the partner's myth visible in the game prompt, both agents have *common-knowledge access to a shared narrative anchor* and resolve the contradiction by coordinating on it (Chwe 2001). The content of the anchor is largely irrelevant; what matters is that there is *one*, that *both* see *the same one*, and that they can *act on it*. Cooperative content provides a modest amplifier; adversarial content does not subtract enough to break the rescue. The competing-prior interpretation in the §3.3 outline is falsified by both arms (visibility rescues, content alone does not). Forward-link to §5.2 for fuller mechanism prose.
